spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Passages

---

** ¶3. ** And great is this interior truth you have sought — whence ar ises the profound de light of good within me, on account of the divine truth I bring forth into expression . It becomes more fully realized when it passes from interior understanding into out ward communication than when it r ests within the will alone . You yourself enter into spiritual delight through it; and whoever receives it from you shall likewise enter into that de light, and be illumin ated by wisdom , and receive from it a power that does not per ish.

**¶4. ** For consider how this matter stands : it is as when a living truth is first conceived within the interior understanding . It turns and grows within the deeper mind, filling the whole of the inner life . The understanding perce ives and recogn izes that this truth it has received is alive within it, and there is de light over it until the time when it is brought forth into the light . And it comes forth whole , with every faculty complete and perfect in spiritual form , without dist ortion — into the open sphere of conscious awareness, which is far more expans ive than the enclosed interior state in which it first existed. The fac ulties of perception are filled with wisdom , and it speaks with a living power of expression , after the manner of all tru ths that are born into the world of use .

**¶5.** Now, at the time when the understanding first receives a truth within itself, the delight of that interior reception is not nearly so great as when the truth is brought forth and its full form is perceived — when one is filled with its beauty and complet eness in a single act of recognition . The love and delight over it become a hund redfold greater than before , now that truth has come into manifest expression and is beh eld in its fullness.

**¶6 .** For at first , when truth was held only within the interior understanding, its spiritual form and the light of its perception were hidden from the mind that carried it. But when it was brought forth into expression , its form was seen . Its full ness and lo veliness came before the perception of the good from which it originated and the understanding that bore it and all the kindred affections of the interior life . And they enter into ever -deep ening delight as they be hold it directly , perce iving its spiritual form and the joy it communic ates without med iation.

**¶7. ** So it is with this lik eness: divine truth present within the will of a person is like the living truth conceived within the interior understanding. And when it is received through instruction and sealed within the will , it becomes as the truth that is brought forth into life , and all perce ive its spiritual beauty.

**¶8.** In this manner , the divine truth that a person brings forth, speaking it out ward from the will , grows and is perfected more and more. Its ex alt ation and glory are multipl ied from the moment when the beauty and splendor of the expressed truth are displayed before the perception of those who receive it. And it advances likewise within you: you perceive through your own reception what you did not know you possessed , and you are astonished at the truth you yourself bring forth.

**¶9. ** Consider again : divine truth, while it remains hidden in the will , before it has been expressed , is like the living power of love conce aled within natural knowledge. That natural knowledge is in ward ly kind led by the love within it , yet the out ward form of the love that exists within the natural knowing is not apparent. You may gather all the natural knowledge you will and place it within a single mind . It is impossible for that mind to be illuminated so long as the wisdom within it remains lat ent and un aw akened — until the time when that knowledge is brought into contact with love , and wisdom comes forth from it. Then it is possible for the entire mind to be illuminated by the wisdom kind led from even a single truth .

**¶10.** This also is the condition of divine truth held within the will of a person. It is like love hidden within natural knowledge, whose wisdom is not yet made visible . The truth is like this : its illumin ation is conce aled, its glory is hidden in the interior life . But when the person brings it forth into expression, its glory is displayed before the perception and the reception of a multitude.

**¶13 .** For in this respect, divine truth is like the living truth of which I have told you, the one brought forth from the understanding . When it is brought forth, the orig inating good and the bearing understanding and the whole circle of kindred affections enter into delight over it. However , there are others who are grieved by it , because they are alien to it. These are not counted among its kindred aff ections. They do not enter into delight, because it does not belong to their spiritual quality .

**¶14.** This is also the condition of divine truth . When it is brought forth through the communication of one who teaches , those who possess an affinity with it receive it into themselves and enter into delight. But those who are spiritu ally alien to it neither de light in it nor receive it into themselves.

**¶15. ** It is as with the wisdom kind led from love within natural knowledge, of which I have spoken to you, which comes forth and is made manifest out wardly before the perception of all . Whoever poss esses spiritual sight beh olds the wisdom that has come forth. But whoever is without interior perception does not see it .

**¶16.** This is also the condition of divine truth when it is commun icated. The person in whom dw ells the interior rational faculty — to that person the truth belongs . Whenever such a one encounters it, that one receives it in wardly. But the one who has no interior rational faculty is alien to it. That one neither receives it inwardly, nor is able to attend to it at all.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Well [do] you ask! And great is this lesson for which you have sought, [that is] whence comes my great joy, on account of this wis-dom that I utter? [For truly,] it is superior in my mouth when I proclaim it than when it is set in m[y heart]. You yourself rejoice in it; and the other one who hears it from you, he shall rejoice in it, and be enlightened [by] it and receive thereby permanent strength.

For like this matter, just so a small b[o]y who is conceived in the belly of his mother. He [grows and he] turns in his mother's womb, filling her womb. The mother knows and understands that this child she conceives is alive within her. She rejoices over him until [the tim]e when she gives birth. And he comes from her alive with his [limbs whole] and perfect in beauty, without defect, [in] the living open air that is more sp[ac]ious than the first air he was in. He fills his eyes with the light and speaks with his living voice in the way of they who are born.

Now, the time when this woman conceives the child in her belly, her joy at conceiving him in her womb is not so [ve]ry great as when she gives birth and sees him; and is full of his [be]auty and stature in the space of a single moment. The love and joy over him shall be a hundred [t]imes greater than it was, now that she has given birth and seen him.

For the first time when she conceived him in her belly, his beauty and the sight of his eyes was hidden from his m[oth]er; but when she gave birth to him she saw his beauty. His s[t]ature and his loveliness came before the e[ye]s of his f[athe]r [a]nd his mother and all his relatives. They shall rejoic[e] over him more and more when they look upon him face to face and see his beauty and delightfulness.

Just as in this simile, the wisdom that is present [in] the heart of the person is like the living child who is co[nceived] in the belly of his mother. And when he is taught and seals it in his heart, it becomes like the child who shall be born, and they see his beauty.

Once again, the wisdom is like this, while it is hidden in the heart of the person. [Bef]ore he has uttered it, it is just like [the blaze] of fire that is hidden in wood. An[d] that wood is [kindled] by the blaze of the fire, but the garment of fir[e that exists in] the wood is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [many pieces of] wood and they put them in a single house. It is impossible to [give li]ght to that house as long as the light within [them is hidden,] until the time when they are added to the fire, and the light [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood.

This is also the case with the wisdom that is in the heart of the person. [It] is like the fire that is hidden in the wood, as its light is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the wisdom is like this: its li[ght] is hidden and its glory is hidden in the heart; but when the person will proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed before the eyes and the ears of a multitude.

For in this respect the wisdom is like this child about whom I have told you, the one who [was] born from the woman. Now, when he will be born, his father and mother and family circle shall rejoice over him. However, you find others grieving by reason of him, [s]ince they are strangers to him. These are not reckoned among his family. [They do n]ot rejoice over him, because he is not of their race.

This is also [the case] with the wisdom. When it is proclaimed by the mouth of the teacher, these who are [a]kin to it shall receive it to them and rejoice in it; but [those] who are strangers to it neither rejoice in it [nor are enlightened by it,] nor receive it to them.

Just like the light of [the fire, which I] proclaim[ed] to you, that shall come from the wood [and be apparent o]utside before the eyes of every one. So, [wh]oever looks shall see the light that has [come fro]m the wood; but whoever is blind does not see the [fir]e.

This is also the case with the wisdom, when it will be pro-claimed. The person, in whom is the [Mi]nd, of him is the wisdom. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it in to him; but the one who has no Mind in him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it in to him, nor shall he listen to [it].

So, in this way, the wisdom that the person proclaims, speak[ing] it from his heart, shall be advanced more and mor[e]. Its en-hancement and glory shall double from the time when the bea-uty and splendour of the saying will be displayed before the eyes [of t]hey who hear it, and it shall also advance for you [the more through] your hearing, and you are astonished at what you proclai[m].
